note: Locked constants a checker enforces. Each cites the ledger directive that created it. Prose is not a constant; if it is not here it is not enforced.

testimonial_shape.why: A short testimonial is one quote in one font, like Barbara's. A long testimonial keeps its lead line and its paragraph. The fix was only ever Debra's; generalising it broke Srini on home-t8.
testimonial_shape.unfiled: The Srini exception (a long testimonial keeps its lead line and its paragraph) is a real correction with no ledger row yet; it is enforced from here until it is filed.

no_numbered_section_labels.why: The numbered eyebrow labels (01 Voices, 02 Your Unique Frequencies) are system furniture a visitor does not need.

no_call_to_action.why: No button in the nav, under the hero, or at the close on the home page. No violet fill.

hero_frame.why: The hero is the one place a stranger sees the product. Three separate lineages shipped a retired hero because nothing stopped them.
hero_frame.acceptance_test: The lady in the cream knitted sweater, with a real modern iPhone at true 19.5:9 proportion, at believable size in her hand, carrying the current real app screen.
hero_frame.screen_source: P-208 The Phone, Frame 04 Build (carrying iPhone Real Screen 01 under the bezel frame); never a separate screen paste
forbidden: a sleeveless tank top on the hero woman
a drawn or warped phone in place of a photographed one

hero_device_plate.why: A phone on a page is the registered device-plate frame, never a painted or warped phone. fd-073 (2026-09-06): the device is THE WHOLE PHONE built the App Store Frame 04 way (real screen UNDER the bezel frame at rx 118, island as hardware, 1920 wide, whole body); P-178 retired for a square screenshot pasted over the bezel.
forbidden: a screenshot pasted on top of the bezel
the body below 1920 px wide before the final scene resize
P-178 or any derivative of it

retired_is_unreachable.why: The library is the gate. A retired number may stay on the pages that already carried it and may never appear anywhere new.
retired_is_unreachable.enforced_by: python3 code/check_design_qa.py asset-ids  (rule 4, RETIRED NUMBER IN NEW USE)
retired_is_unreachable.retired_design_room_frames_why: fd-070, fd-071 (2026-09-06): P-184 was P-160's cut scene with a warped screenshot on a painted phone, never filed in the library; P-182 carried its pop on a coffee cup. Replacements built by workers, filed in the library 8-6, live on home-t11.

bad_picture_never_stands.why: Michael 2026-09-04: "never let a bad picture stand . they get archived to never use or we get this junk". Marking a number retired is half the job; the picture has to come off every live surface and the file has to stop being reachable, or the next builder copies whatever the base is actually serving.
procedure: 1. Add the number to `retired` in brand/site-asset-index.json.

2. Re-plate EVERY live surface that shows it to the replacement, in the same session. Live surfaces are the pages listed in build_asset_index.py PAGES: the library, the styleguide, the control, and the current design-room rounds.
3. Move its file out of the working namespace to site/assets/_retired/ with `git mv`, UNLESS a frozen historical round still references it - those keep what they shipped.
4. Rebuild the index and run the gate. The number must report NOT IN USE on every live page.
5. Negative-test it: point a live page back at the retired file and confirm the gate fails, then revert.
bad_picture_never_stands.live_surfaces_are_gated_by: code/build_asset_index.py PAGES - a surface missing from that list is ungated, and that is how P-163 and P-164 stayed on /site/styleguide after the library had dropped them
bad_picture_never_stands.known_gap: code/archive.py is scoped to the vault repo and refuses paths in zodiac-pages, so step 3 is a manual `git mv` there until the tool takes a repo root.

file_level_supersession.why: A testimonial number is the PERSON, so a bad portrait cannot be retired without retiring the person - and the retired-NUMBER gate therefore waved Debra's broken portrait straight back onto a live page, green, on the day it was replaced. A bad FILE now dies on its own under a number that stays alive.
file_level_supersession.enforced_by: python3 code/check_design_qa.py asset-ids  (rule 5b, SUPERSEDED FILE IN NEW USE) - and publish preflight runs it
file_level_supersession.semantics: Allowance is per FILE, not per asset, and only ever SHRINKS: a superseded file may stay on the frozen pages that already carried it and may never appear anywhere new. The failure names the replacement and the reason.

what_the_gate_blocks.retired_number: a retired P/G number on any page beyond the frozen ones it already had (rule 4)
what_the_gate_blocks.superseded_file: a specific dead FILE, even under a live person number (rule 5b) - names its replacement
what_the_gate_blocks.unfiled_image: an image on a tracked page with no number (rule 1)
what_the_gate_blocks.missing_file: a page pointing at a file that is not on disk (rule 5) - a broken frame is the same defect as a wrong picture

prove_it_still_bites: Each rule is proved by making it go RED, never by watching it stay green.
1. clean repo: python3 code/check_design_qa.py asset-ids  -> PASS
2. point a live page at assets/d4e/d4e-hero-h8.jpg -> RETIRED NUMBER IN NEW USE
3. point one at assets/_retired/d4k-face-debra-SUPERSEDED.png -> SUPERSEDED FILE IN NEW USE, and publish preflight -> PUBLISH BLOCKED
4. point one at a name that does not exist -> UNFILED IMAGE, then rebuild the index -> FILE MISSING ON DISK
5. restore the page and the index, rebuild, confirm PASS.
bad_picture_never_stands.scraper_note: build_asset_index.py and _design_qa/asset_ids.py each carry their own copy of srcs_of(). Keep them in step - patching only one made the gate report a phantom as UNFILED. Both now drop JS-built srcs: a page writing src={'assets/d4e-wave-' + k + '.png'} had been filed as a real asset under that literal name.

colour_coverage_floor.why: No run longer than one phone screen without a real coloured object. A visitor scrolling a silver page needs the colour to arrive before the page reads as empty; two blank screens in a row is where the page stops being a world and becomes a document.
colour_coverage_floor.real_colour: chroma = max(R,G,B) - min(R,G,B) >= 18 on 0-255, AND max(R,G,B) >= 40 so photographic shadow and the NIGHT sheet are not counted as colour. The two thresholds are named COLOUR_CHROMA_MIN and COLOUR_MIN_VALUE in code/check_page.py.
colour_coverage_floor.min_share_note: 0.2 percent of a 375x812 screen is about 610 px of real colour - a 25x25 patch. Calibrated on home-t9 2026-09-05, where the measurement is bimodal with nothing in between: every screen carrying a coloured object read 0.43 to 8.26 percent, and every screen without one read exactly 0.0000 percent (highest chroma anywhere in that 5,684 px stretch: 15, under the threshold). The floor is set at half the smallest real-object reading so the verdict does not hinge on one picture's bottom edge. Re-measure it, do not guess it.

ladder_alternation.why: No two neighbouring sections share a rung. The ladder is how the page changes rooms; two sections on the same sheet is a join with no light in it, and the reader stops registering the change.
ladder_alternation.resolves: every top-level <section> in DOM order, from the page's own ladder table (#section-id {--sheet:var(--lv-NAME)} and .class {--sheet:...}); a section with no declaration takes the default in background:var(--sheet,var(--lv-day))

ladder_steps.why: The ladder only works if the reader can SEE the change of light. Two rungs closer than 4.5 L* are one sheet with extra CSS, a rung that carries a hue tints every photograph standing on it, and a night under L* 22 stops being a room at night and becomes a hole in the page. T9 shipped all three at once: dawn, sun and day sat inside 1.8 L* of each other and the night was a violet #1A1620 at L* 8.11.
ladder_steps.reads: the five --lv-dawn / --lv-sun / --lv-day / --lv-room / --lv-night hex tokens declared in the page's own CSS. Only a literal hex is read; a rung written as a var() or a colour function is not a measurable step and the rule says so rather than guessing.
ladder_steps.neutral_rule: R must equal G, and B must sit within neutral_tolerance of R. fd-062: never a hue, never a warm pixel. The house pattern is R=G with B one less, which is a chroma of 1; T9's night was a chroma of 10 and read violet on every screen.
ladder_steps.min_step_note: CIELAB L*, sRGB D65, computed in code/check_page.py (_srgb_to_lstar). L* is used and not the hex value because it is perceptual: the same step is the same visible amount of light at the top of the ladder and at the bottom. The four light rungs are SORTED BY LIGHTNESS first and the step is checked between neighbours in that order, so renaming or re-ordering the ladder cannot hide a collapsed pair. Measured 2026-09-05: T10 steps 7.13 / 5.62 / 5.20, T9 steps 8.10 / 1.74 / 0.69.
ladder_steps.night_lstar_note: Photographic night, not pitch black (fd-065). The band is the sky of the bank's own night frames, measured 24-34 on 2026-09-05; the floor sits just under the measured low so a slightly deeper night is still allowed and a void is not, and the ceiling is where night stops reading as night. T10's #40403F measures L* 27.06. Re-measure it against the frames, do not guess it.

night_no_warm_pixels.why: No cream, no warm pixel. The night sheet is the one place a warm cast is invisible to the builder and obvious to the eye - the retired --cream ink, an amber bloom, a candlelit gradient all read as neutral in the CSS and as firelight on the screen. A picture may be warm, because a lamp inside a photograph is the photograph; what may never be warm is the page around it.
night_no_warm_pixels.scope: every top-level <section> on the --lv-night rung, at 375 and 1440, over the full stitched render. A page declares the rung either in the section's own class (class="set-night", the T10 form) or in a table of ids (#results{--sheet:var(--lv-night)}, the T9 form); the checker asks the rendered section for its computed --sheet, so neither form can hide from the rule.
night_no_warm_pixels.warm_pixel: hue on the HSV circle inside hue_band_deg, AND chroma = max(R,G,B) - min(R,G,B) > chroma_min on 0-255. The defaults are named WARM_HUE_LO, WARM_HUE_HI and WARM_CHROMA_MIN in code/check_page.py; these values are the authority.
night_no_warm_pixels.hue_band_note: 15 degrees is past red and 70 is short of green, so the wedge is exactly the cream / amber / gold family and a violet or green cast is another rule's business.
night_no_warm_pixels.chroma_note: 12 sits deliberately UNDER the census's COLOUR_CHROMA_MIN of 18: the census hunts a real coloured OBJECT, this hunts a CAST, and a cast is weaker than an object by definition. MEASURED on 2026-09-05, not guessed, and the measurement is bimodal with nothing in between. On T10's clean night, 99 percent of the section sits at chroma 7 or under and 99.9 percent at 11 or under (the 5 percent grain film is the whole of that spread); only 875 pixels of 1,180,875 clear 11, and every one of them is inside a photograph. On T9's night, every warm pixel outside the pictures measures chroma 13 or 14, and 2,236 of the 2,968 in #study are exactly rgba(246,241,232) - the retired --cream ink, verbatim. The threshold is set at 12 because that is the empty gap between the two.
night_no_warm_pixels.outside_img_only: Warm pixels are counted twice: inside the union of the boxes that intersect the section, and outside it. Only the OUTSIDE count decides the verdict. Every visible counts, with no decorative exemption, because the question is about the page and not about the alt text.
night_no_warm_pixels.fixed_chrome: Localized fixed or sticky chrome is hidden before the capture: the browser paints it once per screen, so a stitched full-length render would carry one copy of it per screen lying across the night. Full-bleed fixed layers - the backdrop plate, the grain film - are kept, because a warm cast one of them lays over the section is exactly the defect this rule names.

retired_credits.why: Michael corrects a person's credit and it binds forward, but a design round is built by copying the previous round, so the retired credit rides along unless a check fails on it. Frozen rounds keep what they shipped; this only runs on the page under check.
